122: +### Reboot
123: +
124: +A reboot issued from within the node, for example with `tools platform chassis reboot`, restarts the SR Linux container. The node comes back with its links, saved configuration and management address intact.

192: +	case clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:
193: +		if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
194: +			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container start error: %w", node, err)
195: +		}

198: +			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container unpause error: %w", node, err)
199: +		}
200: +	case clabruntime.NotFound:

204: +		)
205: +	default:
206: +		return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container %q is %s",
207: +			node, n.Cfg.LongName, status)
208: +	}

211: +}

+

+package nodes
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+
+	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
+	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
+)
+
+// NetnsHolder is an internal container that owns the network namespace of a node. The node's
+// containers join it, so the links and the management address outlive their restarts.
+type NetnsHolder struct {
+	DefaultNode
+}
+
+func (n *NetnsHolder) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...NodeOption) error {
+	n.DefaultNode = *NewDefaultNode(n)
+	n.Cfg = cfg
+	n.StopSignal = clabtypes.SIGTERM
+
+	for _, o := range opts {
+		o(n)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// EnsureRunning starts or unpauses the holder, so that the containers of node can join it.
+func (n *NetnsHolder) EnsureRunning(ctx context.Context, node string) error {
+	switch status := n.GetContainerStatus(ctx); status {
+	case clabruntime.Running:
+	case clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:
+		if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container start error: %w", node, err)
+		}
+	case clabruntime.Paused:
+		if err := n.Runtime.UnpauseContainer(ctx, n.Cfg.LongName); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container unpause error: %w", node, err)
+		}
+	case clabruntime.NotFound:
+		return fmt.Errorf(
+			"node %q network namespace container %q not found; recreate the node",
+			node, n.Cfg.LongName,
+		)
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container %q is %s",
+			node, n.Cfg.LongName, status)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}

+package srl
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"maps"
+
+	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
+	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
+	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
+	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
+)
+
+const netnsNodeType = "srl-netns"
+
+// usesNetnsNode reports whether the node runs in the network namespace of a holder container.
+// Nodes with a user-defined network mode keep the network namespace of their own container.
+func (n *srl) usesNetnsNode() bool {
+	return n.Cfg.NetworkMode == "" && !n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased
+}
+
+func (n *srl) initNetnsNode() error {
+	if !n.usesNetnsNode() {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	n.netnsNode = new(clabnodes.NetnsHolder)
+
+	return n.netnsNode.Init(n.newNetnsConfig(), clabnodes.WithRuntime(n.GetRuntime()))
+}
+
+func (n *srl) newNetnsConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
+	labels := maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Labels)
+
+	if labels == nil {
+		labels = map[string]string{}
+	}
+
+	shortName := n.Cfg.ShortName + "-netns"
+	labels[clabconstants.NodeName] = shortName
+
+	longName := n.Cfg.LongName + "-netns"
+	labels[clabconstants.LongName] = longName
+
+	labels[clabconstants.NodeType] = netnsNodeType
+	labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] = "true"
+
+	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName] = n.Cfg.ShortName
+	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeLongName] = n.Cfg.LongName
+
+	return &clabtypes.NodeConfig{
+		ShortName:             shortName,
+		LongName:              longName,
+		Hostname:              n.Cfg.GetHostname(),
+		Fqdn:                  n.Cfg.Fqdn,
+		LabDir:                n.Cfg.LabDir,
+		Index:                 n.Cfg.Index,
+		Kind:                  n.Cfg.Kind,
+		NodeType:              netnsNodeType,
+		Image:                 n.Cfg.Image,
+		ImagePullPolicy:       n.Cfg.ImagePullPolicy,
+		RestartPolicy:         n.Cfg.RestartPolicy,
+		Sysctls:               maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Sysctls),
+		User:                  "0:0",
+		Entrypoint:            "/bin/sh",
+		Cmd:                   `-c "trap 'exit 0' TERM INT; sleep infinity & wait $!"`,
+		Env:                   map[string]string{},
+		PortBindings:          n.Cfg.PortBindings,
+		PortSet:               n.Cfg.PortSet,
+		MgmtNet:               n.Cfg.MgmtNet,
+		MgmtIntf:              n.Cfg.MgmtIntf,
+		MgmtIPv4Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,
+		MgmtIPv4AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4AddressAuto,
+		MgmtIPv4PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength,
+		MgmtIPv6Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,
+		MgmtIPv6AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6AddressAuto,
+		MgmtIPv6PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,
+		MgmtIPv4Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,
+		MgmtIPv6Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,
+		MacAddress:            n.Cfg.MacAddress,
+		Aliases:               n.Cfg.Aliases,
+		DNS:                   n.Cfg.DNS,
+		ExtraHosts:            n.Cfg.ExtraHosts,
+		Labels:                labels,
+		Runtime:               n.Cfg.Runtime,
+		ResultingPortBindings: n.Cfg.ResultingPortBindings,
+	}
+}
+
+// containerConfig returns the config of the SR Linux container attached to the holder's
+// network namespace. The runtime rejects network settings for such containers, as they
+// belong to the holder.
+func (n *srl) containerConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
+	cfg := *n.Cfg
+	cfg.NetworkMode = "container:" + n.netnsNode.GetShortName()
+	cfg.DNS = nil
+	cfg.ExtraHosts = nil
+	cfg.MacAddress = ""
+	cfg.PortBindings = nil
+	cfg.PortSet = nil
+
+	return &cfg
+}
+
+// linkNetns points the node's netns symlink to the holder, as the namespace path of the
+// SR Linux container changes whenever the container restarts.
+func (n *srl) linkNetns(ctx context.Context) error {
+	nsPath, err := n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	return clabutils.LinkContainerNS(nsPath, n.Cfg.LongName)
+}
+
+// GetNSPath retrieves the Namespace Path.
+func (n *srl) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
+	if n.netnsNode == nil {
+		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+	}
+
+	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+}
+
+// DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes the symlink file created for the container netns.
+func (n *srl) DeleteNetnsSymlink() error {
+	if n.netnsNode == nil {
+		return n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink()
+	}
+
+	return errors.Join(n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink(), n.netnsNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())
+}

+	if n.netnsNode == nil {

+

+		if errors.Is(err, clabnodes.ErrContainersNotFound) {

+		}

+			return cnts, nil
+		}
+
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	cnts[0].NetworkName = holder[0].NetworkName
+	cnts[0].NetworkSettings = holder[0].NetworkSettings
+	cnts[0].Ports = holder[0].Ports

+	return cnts, nil

# Karpathy behavioral guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:

- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:

- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:

- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

---

**These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

21:

27: }

29: // EnsureRunning starts or unpauses the holder, so that the containers of node can join it.
30: func (n *NetnsHolder) EnsureRunning(ctx context.Context, node string) error {
31: 	switch status := n.GetContainerStatus(ctx); status {
32: 	case clabruntime.Running:
33: 	case clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:
34: 		if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
35: 			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container start error: %w", node, err)

40: 		}

44: 			node, n.Cfg.LongName,

48: 			node, n.Cfg.LongName, status)

491: 	log.Info("Running postdeploy actions",
492: 		"kind", n.Cfg.Kind,
493: 		"node", n.Cfg.ShortName)
494: 
495: 	// generate the certificate
496: 	certificate, err := n.LoadOrGenerateCertificate(n.cert, n.topologyName)
497: 	if err != nil {
498: 		return err
499: 	}
500: 
501: 	// set the certificate data
502: 	n.Config().TLSCert = string(certificate.Cert)
503: 	n.Config().TLSKey = string(certificate.Key)
504: 
505: 	// Populate /etc/hosts for service discovery on mgmt interface
506: 	if err := n.populateHosts(ctx, params.Nodes); err != nil {
507: 		log.Warnf("Unable to populate hosts for node %q: %v", n.Cfg.ShortName, err)
508: 	}
509: 
510: 	// start waiting for initial commit and mgmt server ready
511: 	if err := n.Ready(ctx); err != nil {
512: 		return err
513: 	}
514: 
515: 	n.swVersion, err = n.RunningVersion(ctx)
516: 	if err != nil {
517: 		return err
518: 	}
519: 
520: 	n.supportsOpenconfig, err = n.OpenConfigFeatureEnabled(ctx)
521: 	if err != nil {
522: 		return err
523: 	}
524: 
525: 	// return if config file is found in the lab directory.
526: 	// This can be either if the startup-config has been mounted by that path
527: 	// or the config has been previously generated and saved
528: 	if clabutils.FileExists(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "config", "config.json")) {
529: 		return nil
530: 	}
531: 
532: 	if err := n.addDefaultConfig(ctx); err != nil {
533: 		return err
534: 	}
535: 
536: 	if err := n.addOverlayCLIConfig(ctx); err != nil {
537: 		return err
538: 	}
539: 
540: 	// once default and overlay config is added, we can commit the config
541: 	if err := n.commitConfig(ctx); err != nil {
542: 		return err
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	return n.generateCheckpoint(ctx)
546: }

573: // Ready returns when the node boot sequence reached the stage when it is ready to accept config
574: // commands
575: // returns an error if not ready by the expiry of the timer readyTimeout.
576: func (n *srl) Ready(ctx context.Context) error {
577: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, readyTimeout)
578: 	defer cancel()
579: 
580: 	var err error
581: 
582: 	log.Debugf("Waiting for SR Linux node %q to boot...", n.Cfg.ShortName)
583: 
584: 	for {
585: 		select {
586: 		case <-ctx.Done():
587: 			return fmt.Errorf(
588: 				"timed out waiting for SR Linux node %s to boot: %v",
589: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
590: 				err,
591: 			)
592: 		default:
593: 			// two commands are checked, first if the mgmt_server is running
594: 			cmd, _ := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromString(mgmtServerRdyCmd)
595: 
596: 			execResult, err := n.RunExec(ctx, cmd)
597: 			if err != nil || (execResult != nil && execResult.GetReturnCode() != 0) {
598: 				logMsg := "mgmt_server status check failed"
599: 
600: 				if err != nil {
601: 					logMsg += fmt.Sprintf(" error: %v", err)
602: 				}
603: 
604: 				if execResult != nil && execResult.GetReturnCode() != 0 {
605: 					logMsg += fmt.Sprintf(", output: \n%s", execResult)
606: 				}
607: 
608: 				log.Debug(logMsg)
609: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
610: 
611: 				continue
612: 			}
613: 
614: 			if execResult.GetStdErrString() != "" {
615: 				log.Debugf(
616: 					"error during checking SR Linux boot status: %s",
617: 					execResult.GetStdErrString(),
618: 				)
619: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
620: 
621: 				continue
622: 			}
623: 
624: 			if !strings.Contains(execResult.GetStdOutString(), "running") {
625: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
626: 
627: 				continue
628: 			}
629: 
630: 			// once mgmt server is running, we need to check if it is ready to accept configuration
631: 			// commands
632: 			// this is done with checking readyForConfigCmd
633: 			cmd, _ = clabexec.NewExecCmdFromString(readyForConfigCmd)
634: 
635: 			execResult, err = n.RunExec(ctx, cmd)
636: 			if err != nil {
637: 				log.Debugf("error during readyForConfigCmd execution: %s", err)
638: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
639: 
640: 				continue
641: 			}
642: 
643: 			if execResult.GetStdErrString() != "" {
644: 				log.Debugf("readyForConfigCmd stderr: %s", execResult.GetStdErrString())
645: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
646: 
647: 				continue
648: 			}
649: 
650: 			if !strings.Contains(execResult.GetStdOutString(), "loaded initial configuration") {
651: 				log.Debugf(
652: 					"Management server readiness files doesn't contain the marker string %s",
653: 					execResult.GetStdOutString(),
654: 				)
655: 				time.Sleep(retryTimer)
656: 
657: 				continue
658: 			}
659: 
660: 			log.Debugf("Node %s is ready to accept configs", n.Cfg.ShortName)
661: 
662: 			return nil
663: 		}
664: 	}
665: }

697: func (n *srl) createSRLFiles() error {
698: 	log.Debugf("Creating directory structure for SRL container: %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
699: 
700: 	var src string
701: 
702: 	if n.Cfg.License != "" {
703: 		// copy license file to node specific directory in lab
704: 		src = n.Cfg.License
705: 
706: 		licPath := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "license.key")
707: 		if err := clabutils.CopyFile(context.Background(), src, licPath,
708: 			clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
709: 			return fmt.Errorf("CopyFile src %s -> dst %s failed %v", src, licPath, err)
710: 		}
711: 
712: 		log.Debugf("CopyFile src %s -> dst %s succeeded", src, licPath)
713: 	}
714: 
715: 	// generate SRL topology file, including base MAC
716: 	err := generateSRLTopologyFile(n.Cfg)
717: 	if err != nil {
718: 		return err
719: 	}
720: 
721: 	clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "config"),
722: 		clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
723: 
724: 	// create repository files (for yum/apt) that
725: 	// are mounted to srl container during the init phase
726: 	err = n.createRepoFiles()
727: 	if err != nil {
728: 		return err
729: 	}
730: 
731: 	// generate a startup config file
732: 	// if the node has a `startup-config:` statement, the file specified in that section
733: 	// will be used as a template in GenerateConfig()
734: 	var cfgTemplate string
735: 
736: 	cfgPath := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "config", "config.json")
737: 	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig != "" {
738: 		log.Debug("Reading startup-config", "file", n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
739: 
740: 		c, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
741: 		if err != nil {
742: 			return err
743: 		}
744: 
745: 		cBuf, err := clabutils.SubstituteEnvsAndTemplate(bytes.NewReader(c), n.Cfg)
746: 		if err != nil {
747: 			return err
748: 		}
749: 
750: 		// Determine if startup-config is a JSON file
751: 		// Get slice of data with optional leading whitespace removed.
752: 		// See RFC 7159, Section 2 for the definition of JSON whitespace.
753: 		x := bytes.TrimLeft(cBuf.Bytes(), " \t\r\n")
754: 
755: 		isJSON := len(x) > 0 && x[0] == '{'
756: 		if !isJSON {
757: 			log.Debugf(
758: 				"startup-config passed to %s is in the CLI format. Will apply it in post-deploy stage",
759: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
760: 			)
761: 
762: 			n.startupCliCfg = cBuf.Bytes()
763: 
764: 			// no need to generate and mount startup-config passed in a CLI format
765: 			// as we will apply it over the top of a default config in the post deploy stage
766: 			return nil
767: 		}
768: 
769: 		cfgTemplate = cBuf.String()
770: 	}
771: 
772: 	if cfgTemplate == "" {
773: 		log.Debugf(
774: 			"configuration template for node %s is empty, skipping startup config file generation",
775: 			n.Cfg.ShortName,
776: 		)
777: 
778: 		return nil
779: 	}
780: 
781: 	err = n.GenerateConfig(cfgPath, cfgTemplate)
782: 	if err != nil {
783: 		log.Errorf("node=%s, failed to generate config: %v", n.Cfg.ShortName, err)
784: 	}
785: 
786: 	return err
787: }

836: // addDefaultConfig adds srl default configuration such as tls certs, gnmi/json-rpc, login-banner.
837: func (n *srl) addDefaultConfig(ctx context.Context) error {
838: 	b, err := n.banner()
839: 	if err != nil {
840: 		return err
841: 	}
842: 
843: 	var dnsServers []string
844: 	if n.Config().DNS != nil {
845: 		dnsServers = n.Config().DNS.Servers
846: 	}
847: 
848: 	// tplData holds data used in templating of the default config snippet
849: 	tplData := srlTemplateData{
850: 		TLSKey:           n.Cfg.TLSKey,
851: 		TLSCert:          n.Cfg.TLSCert,
852: 		TLSAnchor:        n.Cfg.TLSAnchor,
853: 		Banner:           b,
854: 		IFaces:           map[string]tplIFace{},
855: 		MgmtMTU:          0,
856: 		MgmtIPMTU:        0,
857: 		DNSServers:       dnsServers,
858: 		SNMPConfig:       snmpv2Config,
859: 		GRPCConfig:       grpcConfig,
860: 		OCServerConfig:   "",
861: 		NDKServerConfig:  "",
862: 		DNSServersConfig: "",
863: 	}
864: 
865: 	if err := n.setVersionSpecificParams(&tplData); err != nil {
866: 		return err
867: 	}
868: 
869: 	n.setCustomPrompt(&tplData)
870: 
871: 	// set MgmtMTU to the MTU value of the runtime management network
872: 	// so that the two MTUs match.
873: 	tplData.MgmtIPMTU = n.Runtime.Mgmt().MTU
874: 
875: 	if err := n.populateInterfaceConfig(&tplData); err != nil {
876: 		return err
877: 	}
878: 
879: 	buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
880: 
881: 	err = srlCfgTpl.Execute(buf, tplData)
882: 	if err != nil {
883: 		return err
884: 	}
885: 
886: 	log.Debugf("Node %q additional config:\n%s", n.Cfg.ShortName, buf.String())
887: 
888: 	// Copy overlay config to container
889: 	tmpFilePath, err := clabutils.WriteToTempFile(buf.String())
890: 	if err != nil {
891: 		return err
892: 	}
893: 	defer os.Remove(tmpFilePath)
894: 
895: 	err = n.Runtime.CopyToContainer(ctx, n.Cfg.LongName, defaultCfgPath, tmpFilePath)
896: 	if err != nil {
897: 		return fmt.Errorf("error copying configuration to container: %w", err)
898: 	}
899: 
900: 	// su to admin user to apply the default config
901: 	// to make sure that the 'environment save' command will create
902: 	// files with correct permissions
903: 	cmd := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromSlice([]string{
904: 		"bash", "-c",
905: 		fmt.Sprintf("su -s /bin/bash admin -c '/opt/srlinux/bin/sr_cli -ed < %s'", defaultCfgPath),
906: 	})
907: 
908: 	execResult, err := n.RunExec(ctx, cmd)
909: 	if err != nil {
910: 		return err
911: 	}
912: 
913: 	log.Debugf(
914: 		"node %s. stdout: %s, stderr: %s",
915: 		n.Cfg.ShortName,
916: 		execResult.GetStdOutString(),
917: 		execResult.GetStdErrString(),
918: 	)
919: 
920: 	return nil
921: }

923: // populateInterfaceConfig adds endpoint settings to the default configuration,
924: // returning an error for interface names that cannot be mapped to SR Linux interfaces.
925: func (n *srl) populateInterfaceConfig(tplData *srlTemplateData) error {
926: 	const ethernetSplitParts = 3
927: 
928: 	const ethernetMTUOverhead = 14
929: 
930: 	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
931: 		ifName := e.GetIfaceName()
932: 
933: 		// Runtime-discovered endpoints bypass topology interface-name validation.
934: 		if !normalizedInterfaceRegexp.MatchString(ifName) {
935: 			return fmt.Errorf(
936: 				"invalid SR Linux interface %q: expected %s or %s",
937: 				ifName, mgmt0InterfaceName, InterfaceHelp,
938: 			)
939: 		}
940: 
941: 		// Restored runtime endpoints may have no topology link or configured MTU.
942: 		mtu := clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
943: 		if link := e.GetLink(); link != nil {
944: 			mtu = link.GetMTU()
945: 		}
946: 
947: 		if ifName == mgmt0InterfaceName {
948: 			if mtu != clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU {
949: 				tplData.MgmtMTU = mtu
950: 				tplData.MgmtIPMTU = mtu - ethernetMTUOverhead
951: 			}
952: 
953: 			continue
954: 		}
955: 
956: 		ifNameParts := strings.SplitN(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, "e"), "-", ethernetSplitParts)
957: 
958: 		iface := tplIFace{}
959: 
960: 		iface.BaseName = fmt.Sprintf("ethernet-%s/%s", ifNameParts[0], ifNameParts[1])
961: 		if len(ifNameParts) == ethernetSplitParts {
962: 			iface.FullName = fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", iface.BaseName, ifNameParts[2])
963: 			iface.HasBreakout = true
964: 		} else {
965: 			iface.FullName = iface.BaseName
966: 		}
967: 
968: 		if mtu != clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU {
969: 			iface.Mtu = mtu
970: 		}
971: 
972: 		if a := e.GetIPv4Addr(); a.IsValid() {
973: 			iface.IPv4 = a.String()
974: 		}
975: 
976: 		if a := e.GetIPv6Addr(); a.IsValid() {
977: 			iface.IPv6 = a.String()
978: 		}
979: 
980: 		tplData.IFaces[ifName] = iface
981: 	}
982: 
983: 	return nil
984: }

6. How the netns holder container appears in `inspect`, `deploy` output, `clab` node registry — is `srl-netns` a registered node kind? The holder is a `NetnsHolder` node not in the registry, but it's not part of `CLab.Nodes` presumably; only the srl node has the netnsNode field. How does deploy discovery/resolution work for filters (`--node` filters, node filtering)? The holder isn't registered as a node in the lab, so destroy filters etc. operate on the srl node only; Delete handles holder.
7. `CheckInterfaceOverlap`/management IP: the holder takes the node's mgmt IP; the srl container runs in `container:` mode. Does the runtime handle `container:` network mode with MgmtIPv4Address etc.? The `containerConfig()` clears DNS/ExtraHosts/MacAddress/PortBindings/PortSet but keeps MgmtIPv4Address etc. Would the docker runtime reject mgmt IP with container network mode? The comment says "The runtime rejects network settings for such containers" — but they only cleared DNS, ExtraHosts, MacAddress, port bindings... What about MgmtIPv4Address? Let me check the runtime CreateContainer implementation to see what it does with `container:` network mode and mgmt IPs.

Actually, wait — the holder gets MgmtIPv4Address of the node. But the node's own mgmt IP is what's used in PostDeploy etc. The holder gets the mgmt IP, and the srl container joins the holder's netns, so the mgmt interface belongs to the netns. So the holder carries the mgmt IP config. OK.

8. Restart policy: srl default "unless-stopped". Note the holder inherits the node's RestartPolicy. But `Stop` explicitly stops the holder; with `unless-stopped`, after a manual stop the docker daemon won't restart it — good. But wait: when srl container reboots (exits), docker restarts it (unless-stopped), and the holder stays running, so the new srl container... hmm, actually the container restarts in place (same container restarted by runtime), so netns path stays? Actually restart of a docker container keeps the same netns? On restart, the container's netns is recreated? Actually when a container exits and restarts, the network namespace persists? For docker, on restart the netns object may be recreated. The netns symlink points to holder anyway, so fine.

11. `runtime_state.go`: `runtimeContainerLess` sorts internal first. Where is it used? Sorting containers in groups for deletion. Check `runtimeNodeGroups` in core/runtime_state.go and how deletion order matters. Also does destroy/deploy listing now show the holder container with the node name "srl1-netns"? `runtimeContainerNodeName` uses NodeName label; the holder's NodeName label is "srl1-netns" while RootNodeName is "srl1". In the test, group key "srl1" contains both containers. How? Let's read core/runtime_state.go fully.

12. Also check `clab` labels: the holder gets `containerlab` label cloned from node? Yes, maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Labels) — includes containerlab label = lab name presumably, so destroy --cleanup filters by lab label; the test verifies no lab containers left. Good.

13. Check `nodes/srl/netns_test.go` references `n.Cfg.RestartPolicy` default "unless-stopped" — set in Init. TestUserNetworkModeSkipsNetnsNode expects RestartPolicy still set — yes.

14. Schema: restart policy is a string field; no schema change needed? The `restart-policy` default change is kind-specific, not schema. But wait: does the schema for srl kind define default restart-policy? Check clab.schema.json for restart policy enum/defaults. The schema may enumerate restart policies; "unless-stopped" likely included. No schema change needed since it's a code default. But docs updated.

15. Docs: srl.md reboot section added; nodes.md updated restart policy default mention. The docs claim "The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`". Check inspect --all behavior: does inspect have an --all flag that includes internal containers? Need to check cmd inspect. If the claim is wrong, docs bug. 18. Potential issue in `Stop`: `n.DefaultNode.Stop(ctx)` stops the srl container; then if holder running, stop holder. But DefaultNode.Stop may already return nil early if container not running. Fine.

However: `Stop` semantics — stopping the holder kills the netns; when node restarts (Start), EnsureRunning starts holder. But with restart policy "unless-stopped", if a user runs `docker stop clab-...-srl1` only (not the holder), docker won't restart the holder... The docs say use clab commands.

But wait: is that true for podman too? Likely yes.

If the docker runtime's CreateContainer with NetworkMode container:... attempts to attach with IP config, it would error. 244: func runtimeComponentSortOrder(name string) int {
245: 	idx := strings.LastIndex(name, "-")
246: 	if idx < 0 || idx == len(name)-1 {
247: 		return 0
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	slot := strings.ToUpper(name[idx+1:])
251: 	if len(slot) == 1 && slot[0] >= 'A' && slot[0] <= 'Z' {
252: 		return 100 - int(slot[0])
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	var n int
256: 	for _, r := range slot {
257: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
258: 			return 0
259: 		}

394: 	}
395: 
396: 	action := diff.DefaultAction()
397: 	result.Action = action
398: 
399: 	switch action {
400: 	case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart:
401: 		result.Restarted = []string{d.Cfg.LongName}
402: 	case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRecreate:
403: 		result.Recreated = []string{d.Cfg.LongName}
404: 	}
405: 
406: 	return result
407: }

416: // Reconcile applies the diff and executes the appropriate action (restart/recreate).
417: func (d *DefaultNode) Reconcile(
418: 	ctx context.Context,
419: 	diff *clabtypes.TopologyDiff,
420: ) (*ReconcileResult, error) {
421: 	result := d.ComputeReconcilePlan(diff)
422: 
423: 	if result.Action == clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionNone {
424: 		return result, nil
425: 	}
426: 
427: 	log.Info(
428: 		"Applying node changes",
429: 		"node",
430: 		d.Cfg.ShortName,
431: 		"action",
432: 		result.Action,
433: 		"fields",
434: 		diff.Fields,
435: 	)
436: 
437: 	switch result.Action {
438: 	case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart:
439: 		if err := d.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
440: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("stop failed: %w", err)
441: 		}
442: 		if err := d.Start(ctx); err != nil {
443: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("start failed: %w", err)
444: 		}
445: 
446: 	case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRecreate:
447: 		if err := d.Delete(ctx); err != nil {
448: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("delete failed: %w", err)
449: 		}
450: 	}
451: 
452: 	return result, nil
453: }

590: // CalculateInterfaceIndex parses the supplied interface name with the InterfaceRegexp.
591: // Using the the port offset, it calculates the mapped interface index based on the InterfaceOffset
592: // and the first data interface index.
593: func (d *DefaultNode) CalculateInterfaceIndex(ifName string) (int, error) {
594: 	captureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(d.InterfaceRegexp, ifName)
595: 	if err != nil {
596: 		return 0, err
597: 	}
598: 
599: 	if parsedIndex, found := captureGroups["port"]; found {
600: 		parsedIndexInt, err := strconv.Atoi(parsedIndex)
601: 		if err != nil {
602: 			return 0, fmt.Errorf(
603: 				"%q parsed index %q could not be cast to an integer",
604: 				ifName,
605: 				parsedIndex,
606: 			)
607: 		}
608: 		calculatedIndex := parsedIndexInt - d.InterfaceOffset + d.FirstDataIfIndex
609: 		return calculatedIndex, nil
610: 	} else {
611: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf(
612: 			"%q does not have extracted interface index with regexp %q, 'port' capture group missing?",
613: 			ifName,
614: 			d.InterfaceRegexp,
615: 		)
616: 	}
617: }

619: // GetMappedInterfaceName returns with a mapped interface name based on the mapped interface prefix
620: // and calculated mapped interface index.
621: func (d *DefaultNode) GetMappedInterfaceName(ifName string) (string, error) {
622: 	ifIndex, err := d.OverwriteNode.CalculateInterfaceIndex(ifName)
623: 	if err != nil {
624: 		return "", err
625: 	}
626: 	if ifIndex < d.FirstDataIfIndex {
627: 		return "", fmt.Errorf(
628: 			"extracted interface index for %q is out of bounds: %d ! >= %d",
629: 			ifName,
630: 			ifIndex,
631: 			d.FirstDataIfIndex,
632: 		)
633: 	}
634: 	mappedIfName := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", d.InterfaceMappedPrefix, ifIndex)
635: 
636: 	return mappedIfName, nil
637: }

655: // GenerateConfig generates configuration for the nodes
656: // out of the template `t` based on the node configuration and saves the result to dst.
657: // If the config file is already present in the node dir we do not regenerate the config unless
658: // EnforceStartupConfig is explicitly set to true and startup-config points to a file this will
659: // persist the changes that users make to a running config when booted from some startup config.
660: func (d *DefaultNode) GenerateConfig(dst, t string) error {
661: 	// Check for incompatible options
662: 	if d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && d.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {
663: 		return ErrIncompatibleOptions
664: 	}
665: 	if d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && d.Cfg.StartupConfig == "" {
666: 		return ErrNoStartupConfig
667: 	}
668: 
669: 	if d.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {
670: 		log.Info("Startup config generation suppressed", "node", d.Cfg.ShortName)
671: 		return nil
672: 	}
673: 
674: 	if !d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && clabutils.FileExists(dst) {
675: 		log.Debug("Existing config found", "node", d.Cfg.ShortName, "path", dst)
676: 		return nil
677: 	} else {
678: 		log.Debug("Generating config", "node", d.Cfg.ShortName, "file", d.Cfg.StartupConfig)
679: 
680: 		cfgBuf, err := clabutils.SubstituteEnvsAndTemplate(strings.NewReader(t), d.Cfg)
681: 		if err != nil {
682: 			return err
683: 		}
684: 		log.Debug("Generated config", "node", d.Cfg.ShortName, "content", cfgBuf.String())
685: 
686: 		f, err := os.Create(dst)
687: 		if err != nil {
688: 			return err
689: 		}
690: 		defer f.Close()
691: 
692: 		_, err = f.Write(cfgBuf.Bytes())
693: 		if err != nil {
694: 			return err
695: 		}
696: 	}
697: 
698: 	return nil
699: }

724: // LoadStartupConfigFileVr templates a startup-config using the file specified for VM-based nodes in

727: func LoadStartupConfigFileVr(node Node, configDirName, startupCfgFName string) error {
728: 	nodeCfg := node.Config()

730: 	clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Join(nodeCfg.LabDir, configDirName),
731: 		clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)

735: 		dstCfg := filepath.Join(nodeCfg.LabDir, configDirName, startupCfgFName)

737: 		c, err := os.ReadFile(nodeCfg.StartupConfig)

742: 		cfgTemplate := string(c)

745: 		if err != nil {
746: 			log.Errorf("node=%s, failed to generate config: %v", nodeCfg.ShortName, err)
747: 		}
748: 	}
749: 	return nil

854: // LoadOrGenerateCertificate loads a certificate using a certificate storage provider
855: // provided in certInfra or generates a new one if it does not exist.
856: func (d *DefaultNode) LoadOrGenerateCertificate(
857: 	certInfra *clabcert.Cert,
858: 	topoName string,
859: ) (nodeCert *clabcert.Certificate, err error) {
860: 	// early return if certificate generation is not required
861: 	if d.Cfg.Certificate == nil || !*d.Cfg.Certificate.Issue {
862: 		return nil, nil
863: 	}
864: 
865: 	nodeConfig := d.Cfg
866: 
867: 	// try loading existing certificates from disk and generate new ones if they do not exist
868: 	nodeCert, err = certInfra.LoadNodeCert(nodeConfig.ShortName)
869: 	if err != nil {
870: 		log.Debugf("creating node certificate for %s", nodeConfig.ShortName)
871: 
872: 		hosts := []string{
873: 			nodeConfig.ShortName,
874: 			nodeConfig.LongName,
875: 			nodeConfig.ShortName + "." + topoName + ".io",
876: 		}
877: 		// add the SANs provided via config
878: 		hosts = append(hosts, nodeConfig.Certificate.SANs...)
879: 
880: 		// add mgmt IPs as SANs to CSR
881: 		for _, ip := range []string{d.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address, d.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address} {
882: 			if ip != "" {
883: 				hosts = append(hosts, ip)
884: 			}
885: 		}
886: 
887: 		certInput := &clabcert.NodeCSRInput{
888: 			CommonName:   nodeConfig.ShortName + "." + topoName + ".io",
889: 			Hosts:        hosts,
890: 			Organization: "containerlab",
891: 			Country:      "US",
892: 			KeySize:      d.Cfg.Certificate.KeySize,
893: 			Expiry:       d.Cfg.Certificate.ValidityDuration,
894: 		}
895: 		// Generate the cert for the node
896: 		nodeCert, err = certInfra.GenerateAndSignNodeCert(certInput)
897: 		if err != nil {
898: 			return nil, err
899: 		}
900: 
901: 		// persist the cert via certStorage
902: 		err = certInfra.StoreNodeCert(nodeConfig.ShortName, nodeCert)
903: 		if err != nil {
904: 			return nil, err
905: 		}
906: 	}
907: 
908: 	return nodeCert, nil
909: }

941: func (d *DefaultNode) AddLinkToContainer(
942: 	ctx context.Context,
943: 	link netlink.Link,
944: 	f func(ns.NetNS) error,
945: ) error {
946: 	if !d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {
947: 		st := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)
948: 		if !clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(st) {
949: 			if st == clabruntime.Stopped {
950: 				containerName := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName()
951: 				d.GetRuntime().LogNonRunningContainerOutput(ctx, containerName)
952: 			}
953: 			return fmt.Errorf(
954: 				"node %q: cannot attach link, container network namespace is not available (status=%s)",
955: 				d.Cfg.ShortName,
956: 				st,
957: 			)
958: 		}
959: 	}
960: 	// retrieve nodes nspath
961: 	nsp, err := d.OverwriteNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
962: 	if err != nil {
963: 		return err
964: 	}
965: 	// retrieve the namespace handle
966: 	netns, err := ns.GetNS(nsp)
967: 	if err != nil {
968: 		return err
969: 	}
970: 	// move veth endpoint to namespace
971: 	if err := netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(netns.Fd())); err != nil {
972: 		return err
973: 	}
974: 	// execute the given function
975: 	err = netns.Do(f)
976: 	if err != nil {
977: 		return err
978: 	}
979: 	return nil
980: }

982: // ExecFunction executes the given function in the nodes network namespace.
983: func (d *DefaultNode) ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {
984: 	if !d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {
985: 		st := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)

parts.text:
Key observations so far:

1. `srl.Deploy` bypasses `DefaultNode.Deploy` entirely and calls `CreateContainer` + `StartContainer` directly. Note DefaultNode.Deploy also sets `CLAB_INTFS` env (done in srl.Deploy) and sets state Deployed (done). OK. But it does not call `PostDeploy` — PostDeploy is separate. Fine.

Wait, srl.Deploy: `n.Cfg.Env[clabconstants.ClabEnvIntfs] = ...` — set before CreateContainer. Good.

2. The test `TestDeleteRemovesNetnsNode` in netns_test.go: `n.Delete(ctx)` → DefaultNode.Delete iterates endpoints (none), checks GetContainerStatus → the mock expects GetContainerStatus(ctx, testNodeName) → Running, then DeleteContainer. Then netnsNode.Delete → DefaultNode.Delete for the holder: iterates endpoints (none), GetContainerStatus(ctx, testNetnsName) → Running, DeleteContainer. Matches the test. Good.

But note: `n.Delete(ctx)` — srl.Delete calls `n.DefaultNode.Delete(ctx)`. DefaultNode.Delete uses `d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)` → OverwriteNode is `n` (the srl), and srl doesn't override GetContainerStatus, so it uses DefaultNode.GetContainerStatus → GetContainerName → LongName. OK.

3. Important potential issue: `srl.Delete` — holder deletion via `n.netnsNode.Delete(ctx)`. NetnsHolder embeds DefaultNode but does NOT define NodeOverwrites... wait, `NewDefaultNode(n)` requires NodeOverwrites interface. NetnsHolder embeds DefaultNode, which implements all NodeOverwrites methods (VerifyStartupConfig, CheckInterfaceName, CalculateInterfaceIndex, GetMappedInterfaceName, VerifyHostRequirements, PullImage, GetImages, GetContainers, GetContainerName, GetContainerStatus, VerifyContainerName, VerifyLicenseFileExists, PreStop, RunExec, GetNSPath). Since NetnsHolder embeds DefaultNode, its methods satisfy NodeOverwrites. But `GetNSPath` on NetnsHolder — DefaultNode.GetNSPath uses `d.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName())`. OverwriteNode points to the NetnsHolder itself (n). So GetNSPath(holder name) — fine.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `srl.GetNSPath` override returns the holder's NS path when netnsNode != nil. That's used for links pointing at the srl node — they now attach to the holder's netns, which is what we want (persistent across srl container restarts). Good.

4. Now think about `srl.Stop`: DefaultNode.Stop calls ParkEndpoints — this parks endpoints into a parking netns before stopping. Then it stops the srl container. Then srl.Stop stops the holder. When the holder is stopped, the netns dies; the parked veth endpoints were moved to the parking netns (host-named netns), so they survive. Then Start: EnsureRunning starts the holder, DefaultNode.Start starts srl container, RestoreEndpoints moves endpoints back from parking netns into the node netns (via GetNSPath → holder's path). Then linkNetns re-links. OK — this interplay seems handled.

But wait: does Start of the holder re-attach it to the mgmt network with the same IP? Docker `start` of an existing container reuses its network config (static IP if set). Fine.

But an important question: what about the srl container itself being restarted by the runtime (reboot)? The whole premise: the srl container has `network-mode: container:<holder>`, restart policy unless-stopped. When rebooted, it exits, docker restarts it, it joins the holder's netns again, its mgmt IP persists. Good.

5. Potential issue: `EnsureRunning` when status is Paused → Unpause. Then srl.Start proceeds. Fine.

6. Potential issue: `srl.Start` when the srl container status is Running — DefaultNode.Start skips and returns nil; then linkNetns runs. OK.

7. Now `core/runtime_state.go` change: `runtimeContainerLess` sorts internal first. But is the group for srl (non-distributed) built correctly? In `runtimeNodeGroups`, the holder container has `NodeName: srl1-netns`, `RootNodeName: srl1`. groupName = RootNodeName = "srl1" → distributed = true! `distributed := groupName != ""` — so for the holder, distributed is set to true, and `group.distributed = group.distributed || distributed` → the group becomes "distributed". This matters: the duplicate check `if !group.distributed && len(group.containers) > 1` won't flag the srl group as duplicates — good, that's intentional so the holder+srl don't trigger the "apply supports only single-container nodes" error.

But wait — marking the group as `distributed` has other effects elsewhere. Let me check what uses `group.distributed`. In the sros distributed case, "distributed" groups are handled by... let me search. `runtimeNodeGroup.distributed` — used in apply logic presumably to group components under one node. If the srl group is now considered "distributed" because RootNodeName is set on the holder container, other apply logic might treat the srl node as a distributed SR-SIM-like node (e.g., expecting componentNodes, waiting for all components, etc.). Need to check usages.

Also `setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime`: it iterates over containers in groups; the holder carries labels cloned from the node — does the node's labels include `NodeMgmtNetBr`? Let me check what clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr is and where it's set. If the srl node's labels contain `clab-node-mgmt-net-br`... Let me check.

Actually wait, in runtimeNodeGroups the holder has RootNodeName set → groupName = "srl1", distributed=true. For a non-distributed srl node, this wrongly marks the group as distributed. Let me find usages of `.distributed`.

8. Also the deletion path: where are groups' containers deleted? `deleteApplyNodes` in core/apply... Let me check the apply code that uses currentNodes groups and deletes containers in sorted order. The test in apply_test.go references `c.deleteApplyNodes(context.Background(), &applyPlan{currentNodes, deletedNodeSet})`. Let me find that function to verify order of deletion (sorted ascending → delete in that order → internal first = deleted first?). Wait, the comment says "internal holders ... sort first to be deleted last". Sorting ascending with internal first means internal containers come first in the slice. If deletion iterates the slice in order and deletes each, internal holders would be deleted FIRST, not last. Unless deletion iterates in reverse. Let me check deleteApplyNodes.

The test asserts `gomock.InOrder(DeleteContainer(srl1), DeleteContainer(srl1-netns))` — node first, holder last. So deletion must iterate in reverse or sort descending. Let me read the deletion code.

Let me grep for runtimeContainerLess and deleteApplyNodes.

 The license file lifts these limitations as well as unlocks chassis-based platform variants and a path to it can be provided with [`license`](../nodes.md#license) directive.
 
+### Reboot
+
+A reboot issued from within the node, for example with `tools platform chassis reboot`, restarts the SR Linux container. The node comes back with its links, saved configuration and management address intact.
+
+To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node.
+
+Use `containerlab stop`, `start` and `restart` to manage the lifecycle of SR Linux nodes instead of restarting the containers with the container runtime directly.
+
+Nodes with a user-defined [`network-mode`](../nodes.md#network-mode) do not use the internal container.
+

+package nodes
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+
+	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
+	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
+)
+
+// NetnsHolder is an internal container that owns the network namespace of a node. The node's
+// containers join it, so the links and the management address outlive their restarts.
+type NetnsHolder struct {
+	DefaultNode
+}
+
+func (n *NetnsHolder) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...NodeOption) error {
+	n.DefaultNode = *NewDefaultNode(n)
+	n.Cfg = cfg
+	n.StopSignal = clabtypes.SIGTERM
+
+	for _, o := range opts {
+		o(n)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// EnsureRunning starts or unpauses the holder, so that the containers of node can join it.
+func (n *NetnsHolder) EnsureRunning(ctx context.Context, node string) error {
+	switch status := n.GetContainerStatus(ctx); status {
+	case clabruntime.Running:
+	case clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:
+		if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container start error: %w", node, err)
+		}
+	case clabruntime.Paused:
+		if err := n.Runtime.UnpauseContainer(ctx, n.Cfg.LongName); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container unpause error: %w", node, err)
+		}
+	case clabruntime.NotFound:
+		return fmt.Errorf(
+			"node %q network namespace container %q not found; recreate the node",
+			node, n.Cfg.LongName,
+		)
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container %q is %s",
+			node, n.Cfg.LongName, status)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}

+package srl
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"maps"
+
+	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
+	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
+	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
+	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
+)
+
+const netnsNodeType = "srl-netns"
+
+// usesNetnsNode reports whether the node runs in the network namespace of a holder container.
+// Nodes with a user-defined network mode keep the network namespace of their own container.
+func (n *srl) usesNetnsNode() bool {
+	return n.Cfg.NetworkMode == "" && !n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased
+}
+
+func (n *srl) initNetnsNode() error {
+	if !n.usesNetnsNode() {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	n.netnsNode = new(clabnodes.NetnsHolder)
+
+	return n.netnsNode.Init(n.newNetnsConfig(), clabnodes.WithRuntime(n.GetRuntime()))
+}
+
+func (n *srl) newNetnsConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
+	labels := maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Labels)
+
+	if labels == nil {
+		labels = map[string]string{}
+	}
+
+	shortName := n.Cfg.ShortName + "-netns"
+	labels[clabconstants.NodeName] = shortName
+
+	longName := n.Cfg.LongName + "-netns"
+	labels[clabconstants.LongName] = longName
+
+	labels[clabconstants.NodeType] = netnsNodeType
+	labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] = "true"
+
+	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName] = n.Cfg.ShortName
+	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeLongName] = n.Cfg.LongName
+
+	return &clabtypes.NodeConfig{
+		ShortName:             shortName,
+		LongName:              longName,
+		Hostname:              n.Cfg.GetHostname(),
+		Fqdn:                  n.Cfg.Fqdn,
+		LabDir:                n.Cfg.LabDir,
+		Index:                 n.Cfg.Index,
+		Kind:                  n.Cfg.Kind,
+		NodeType:              netnsNodeType,
+		Image:                 n.Cfg.Image,
+		ImagePullPolicy:       n.Cfg.ImagePullPolicy,
+		RestartPolicy:         n.Cfg.RestartPolicy,
+		Sysctls:               maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Sysctls),
+		User:                  "0:0",
+		Entrypoint:            "/bin/sh",
+		Cmd:                   `-c "trap 'exit 0' TERM INT; sleep infinity & wait $!"`,
+		Env:                   map[string]string{},
+		PortBindings:          n.Cfg.PortBindings,
+		PortSet:               n.Cfg.PortSet,
+		MgmtNet:               n.Cfg.MgmtNet,
+		MgmtIntf:              n.Cfg.MgmtIntf,
+		MgmtIPv4Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,
+		MgmtIPv4AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4AddressAuto,
+		MgmtIPv4PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength,
+		MgmtIPv6Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,
+		MgmtIPv6AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6AddressAuto,
+		MgmtIPv6PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,
+		MgmtIPv4Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,
+		MgmtIPv6Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,
+		MacAddress:            n.Cfg.MacAddress,
+		Aliases:               n.Cfg.Aliases,
+		DNS:                   n.Cfg.DNS,
+		ExtraHosts:            n.Cfg.ExtraHosts,
+		Labels:                labels,
+		Runtime:               n.Cfg.Runtime,
+		ResultingPortBindings: n.Cfg.ResultingPortBindings,
+	}
+}
+
+// containerConfig returns the config of the SR Linux container attached to the holder's
+// network namespace. The runtime rejects network settings for such containers, as they
+// belong to the holder.
+func (n *srl) containerConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
+	cfg := *n.Cfg
+	cfg.NetworkMode = "container:" + n.netnsNode.GetShortName()
+	cfg.DNS = nil
+	cfg.ExtraHosts = nil
+	cfg.MacAddress = ""
+	cfg.PortBindings = nil
+	cfg.PortSet = nil
+
+	return &cfg
+}
+
+// linkNetns points the node's netns symlink to the holder, as the namespace path of the
+// SR Linux container changes whenever the container restarts.
+func (n *srl) linkNetns(ctx context.Context) error {
+	nsPath, err := n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	return clabutils.LinkContainerNS(nsPath, n.Cfg.LongName)
+}
+
+// GetNSPath retrieves the Namespace Path.
+func (n *srl) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
+	if n.netnsNode == nil {
+		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+	}
+
+	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
+}
+
+// DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes the symlink file created for the container netns.
+func (n *srl) DeleteNetnsSymlink() error {
+	if n.netnsNode == nil {
+		return n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink()
+	}
+
+	return errors.Join(n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink(), n.netnsNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())
+}
